articles.expand: Knot’s line on fiscal discipline matters most for euro zone sovereign spreads, especially French bonds against German Bunds. A president with that view could make investors less willing to bet on a full central bank backstop if French finances get worse, which risks wider spreads during periods of stress. articles.title: Trump out of public view since Wednesday, fuelling speculation on his wherabouts
articles.expand: For markets, this is a non-event as long as the official record keeps showing normal activity. Traders have learned to discount social media speculation about the president’s health, and nothing so far has moved oil, Treasuries or the US dollar on this story. The risk lies in his travel plans. A smooth departure for China would close the story, but an unexplained delay or cancellation would quickly become a factor for markets. With the Iran war still shaping energy prices , any real uncertainty at the top would tend to lift oil’s risk premium and support safe-haven demand for the dollar. --- T...

articles.title: ECB’s Nagel says another rate hike ‘highly probable’ as energy prices push inflation
articles.expand: An explicit signal from the Bundesbank president that further tightening is likely should support the euro and push up short-dated euro zone yields, especially German two-year debt. Because he ties the risk directly to gas and electricity, euro zone rate pricing is now more sensitive to moves in energy markets, so a rise in oil or gas could feed quickly into ECB hike expectations. His comment that the economy has proved resilient also weakens the argument that growth worries will hold the ECB back, which leaves rate-sensitive European equities more exposed. --- Not only open mouths at the ECB:...

The flat employment reading and persistent cost-of-living complaints, however, point to slack that has not yet closed. articles.title: Weekend Fed speak: Collins backs steady, gradual rate hikes, cool on a bigger December move
articles.expand: Collins’s comments push back on the half-point talk that has built since Waller’s remarks and last week’s inflation data. That could trim some of the tail pricing for a larger December move and take a little heat out of the front end of the Treasury curve. Her view that the eventual rate path may be higher cuts the other way, though. It supports the idea of a longer hiking cycle, which keeps the US dollar supported on dips and leaves gold without a clear dovish tailwind. For traders, her message is about the pace of hikes, not when they stop. --- Also: Sunday Fed talk: Schmid says inflation wo...

articles.title: Sunday Fed talk: Schmid says inflation would still be near 3% without energy, Fed has work to do
articles.expand: Schmid’s remarks add weight to hike pricing that is already in place for December . His attack on the “supply shock” argument also makes it harder to make the dovish case for looking through energy-driven inflation. That supports the US dollar and front-end Treasury yields, and it keeps the small tail risk of a half-point move alive. A Fed seen as committed to further tightening has been a headwind for gold throughout this cycle. His view that AI-driven demand will respond to higher rates is also a reminder to rate-sensitive tech valuations that the sector is not exempt from policy. --- Schmid...

articles.title: Aino Bunge: Interest rates should be adjusted gradually in an uncertain situation
articles.expand: “The Swedish economy is recovering on a broad front, and inflation is expected to rise above target next year. This development justifies a tighter monetary policy, and it is likely that interest rates will be raised further over the coming year. However, any future increases must take into account, not least households’, sensitivity to interest rates." These comments were made by First Deputy Governor Aino Bunge, speaking at Swedbank about the Executive Board’s decision to raise the policy rate to 2 per cent.
